newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks end mixed, avoid Dow sell-off.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks end mixed, avoid Dow sell-off.

* Toronto stocks ended mixed on Tuesday, but avoided the sharp sell-off in New York * TSE propped up by banks, oil, media stocks * 102 million shares traded worth C$1.6 billion
Toronto stocks ended mixed on Tuesday as strength in several key groups enabled the Canadian market to resist a sharp sell-off in New York.
The TSE 300 Composite Index rose 9.07 points to close at 6155.05 on volume of 102.3 million shares worth C$1.6 billion.
But the overall market was mixed, with declining stocks outpacing advances 540 to 436 and 289 stocks ending flat.
Interest rate jitters pushed the Dow Jones Industrial Average down more than 66 points.
"Toronto swam against the tide today," said Ira Katzin, an investment adviser with RBC Dominion Securities.
Banking, communications, and energy stocks led gains in 10 of 14 sub-groups. The four weak sectors were precious metals, forestry, base metals and industrial products.
Despite outperforming the Dow today, analysts expect the next few days will be tense for Canadian stocks.
Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan will complete his Humphrey-Hawkins testimony to Congress on Wednesday, followed by key U.S. jobs data on Friday.
Katzin said investors are awaiting any further comments from Greenspan on interest rates and current high stock levels.
--- HOT STOCKS---

* Firmer oil prices pushed several energy stocks higher. Renaissance Energy Ltd rose 1.15 to 40.65. Gulf Canada Resources Ltd, which was added to the TSE's 100 Index on Tuesday, added 0.50 to close at 10.
* Among bank stocks, Bank of Montreal rose 0.50 to 49.95, while Toronto-Dominion Bank improved 0.10 to 38.35.
* Scott Paper Ltd sank 1.55 to 22 after newsprint company Kruger Inc agreed to buy Scott in a deal worth C$450 million.
* WIC Western Communications Ltd class B jumped 0.55 to 24.65 after CanWest Global Communications bought an additional 1.35 million shares of WIC on Tuesday.
